summary: myidsan gains a built-in user manual -- the third app in the suite to adopt the shared domain/shared/manual library, after mymatasan and myseliasan; previously it shipped no manual at all. 9 articles per language (36 files across en/ms/zh/ar) cover what MyIDSan is, signing in for the first time (finding the generated bootstrap password), connecting a relying app (the authorize/code/token hop and its three token lifetimes), users/roles/groups (clearing a pending account), connecting an LDAP/Active Directory directory, second factors and account recovery, sessions and step-up, the audit log, and backup and restore -- compiled into the binary so help always matches the running server and needs no network access. Served publicly under GET /api/manual, /api/manual/bundle, /api/manual/search, /api/manual/{slug}, /api/manual/assets/{name}, mounted on the bare router before any auth middleware and left off the RBAC permission matrix -- myidsan is the server nobody can sign in to when it is misconfigured, and every question its sign-in screen raises is asked by somebody who is not authenticated yet. In the SPA: an ungated Help nav entry opens the full manual; all four pre-session screens (sign-in, forced password change, MFA enrolment, pending-clearance) each carry their own LoginHelpLink pointed at the article that answers that screen's question; the workspace header's contextual '?' follows the active tab (TAB_HELP); the Apps screen gets three HelpButtons on the steps of registering a relying app; and the first-run setup wizard gets a per-step '?' (STEP_HELP). A manualcheck.UIReferences-driven test (TestManualUIReferences, 27 targets) fails the build if a help target names an article or heading anchor that does not exist, and a new TestManualSpecValues asserts the manual's reference tables (sign-in lockout policy, the three OAuth lifetimes, the audit action vocabulary) against the values the server actually uses -- the latter required exporting three previously-unexported TTL constants in apis/federated_auth.go (DefaultAuthCodeTTLSeconds, DefaultAccessTokenTTLSeconds, DefaultFederatedSessionTTLSeconds; values unchanged). Building this manual also surfaced and fixed a real login bug: a 401 carrying password_change_required or mfa_enrollment_required was treated as a lost session, so a fresh install's bootstrap superadmin was logged straight back out of the forced change-password screen before they could type, and the very first sign-in could never be completed.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive only. New HTTP surface (GET /api/manual and its four sub-routes) is unauthenticated by design, serving only shipped, read-only documentation compiled into the binary -- no runtime state, no per-user data, nothing an operator has typed; the shared rate limiter still applies. A new endpoint-catalog seed row (Public tier, /api/manual) is added on next boot; existing installs pick it up automatically with no migration. The exported federated-auth TTL constants keep their prior values (300s/900s/259200s) and existing behavior -- only their Go visibility changed, and no config key changed. The api.js session-loss fix is a strict correctness fix with no config or route change: existing installs that were never hitting the password-change/mfa-enrollment 401 path see no behavior change; installs that were affected now complete the forced-change/enrolment flow instead of being bounced back to sign-in.
